version.changelog:
## Repo Guardian 1.3.0

- Clarified environment variable requirements: `GH_TOKEN` must be set explicitly; the script no longer falls back to `gh auth token`.
- Updated documentation in SKILL.md to emphasize required environment variables and binaries.
- Minor adjustments to requirements and usage sections for improved clarity and safety.
- No functional changes to review workflow or core automation; changes are documentation and configuration-focused.

llm.summary: The skill's code and instructions largely match its stated purpose, but there are inconsistencies between what it declares and what it actually requires (notably missing required env/binary metadata and explicit agent targets), so proceed with caution and verify runtime dependencies and token scopes before use.

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md and scripts clearly require a GitHub token (GH_TOKEN) and call the OpenClaw CLI to dispatch models, plus standard tools (curl, python3, head/wc). The registry metadata lists no required env vars or binaries — this mismatch is incoherent: a PR-review automation legitimately needs GH_TOKEN and an agent CLI, so the metadata omission is a red flag (either the metadata is incomplete or the skill's declared requirements were intentionally under-specified).
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The script and SKILL.md remain within the stated scope (fetch PRs, send diffs to models, post comments, optionally merge). It explicitly transmits PR diffs and file lists to configured OpenClaw agent models (and truncates diffs to 500 lines). This is expected for an LLM-based reviewer, but it means repository code is sent to whatever model endpoints the agent names map to — confirm those agent endpoints/providers are trusted. The script claims GH_TOKEN is never sent to models; that behavior is enforced in code.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only) which limits disk installation risk. However, the runtime script depends on local binaries (openclaw CLI, curl, python3, and common shell utilities) that are not declared in the skill metadata. That omission reduces transparency about what must be present on the host.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requires GH_TOKEN and documents other optional env vars (GUARDIAN_REPO, GUARDIAN_AUTO_MERGE, etc.) but the registry metadata lists none. GH_TOKEN with repo write permissions is reasonable if auto-merge is enabled, but the user must supply a fine-grained token limited to the target repo. The metadata/manifest mismatch about required credentials is a material coherence issue.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-enabled and does not request elevated platform privileges. It doesn't attempt to modify other skills or system-wide settings. The cron suggestion is a user action; the script does not persist credentials or write to global configs.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Before installing or enabling Repo Guardian: 1) Confirm the metadata mismatch — the skill needs GH_TOKEN and local binaries (openclaw, python3, curl) even though the registry lists none. 2) Create a fine-grained GitHub token scoped only to the target repo (read-only if you won't auto-merge; write only if you explicitly enable auto-merge). 3) Verify which OpenClaw agent names (keats, openforge-cloud, openforge-cloud-fallback) map to which model providers in your environment and ensure those providers are trusted (your repo code will be sent to them). 4) Test first in --dry-run with a disposable repo and enable logging/audit to review actions and comments created. 5) Consider leaving GUARDIAN_AUTO_MERGE disabled until you’ve validated behavior, and review the 'skip-guardian' label handling and any edge-case merges. 6) If you want to proceed, update the skill metadata to declare required env vars and binaries so it's clear what the runtime requires.
